title: Riot is ending development of its 2XKO fighting game
summary: Despite its best efforts since launch, the numbers just aren't there.
body: Six months after laying off approximately 80 developers because "overall momentum hasn't reached the level needed to support a team of this size long term," Riot Games has announced that it is ending development of its fighting game 2XKO . Servers for online play will remain available and the game is also playable offline, but "active development will conclude at the end of 2026." "Over the last few months, we've been monitoring 2XKO's trajectory closely, and what we've seen is painting a clear, consistent picture: while a lot of you jumped in to try the game and there's an incredible community that plays every day, we haven't seen enough players stick with the game to get to a path toward sustainability," Riot wrote in today's update . New content will continue to flow through the remainder of the year, including two new fighters, along with new bug fixes and "feature improvements" leading to a final bug fix patch in December. All fighters are being unlocked, and any money spent on the game "on or before August 20"—that's today—will be refunded. title: This wild new PC pro controller runs its own custom OS across a 2.79-inch color display slapped beneath the thumbsticks
summary: Genki says it is "Beyond the Pro Controller".
body: As $70-$100 controllers are only getting more and more impressive, you might be wondering what the pro controller market can do to make you spend that extra $100 or so. It turns out the answer might be to shove a screen on it. Ain't that always the way? That's what you will find on the Genki Manta, a new controller live on Kickstarter . It uses Manta OS, which is Genki's own operating system, and if you're wondering why a controller would even need an operating system, Genki notes that this allows on-the-fly fine-tuning without the need for any extra devices. You can customise its tri-stage triggers, adjust dead zones, change haptic feedback, and more via the onboard screen and OS. And the controller is pretty impressive even outside the whole 'OS and built-in screen' thing. You get up to 8,000 Hz polling while wired (though only 1,000 Hz via 2.4 GHz wireless), a range of over 10 meters, 150 hours of battery via Bluetooth LE 6, as well as TMR joysticks and Hall effect triggers. The 16 MB of internal storage can be used to load apps onto Manta OS, and expandable storage might be offered as a stretch goal, according to Genki. Normally I'm pretty cynical about Kickstarter projects, b…

title: The latest GTA 6 leak confirms the leaker likely has or had access to a playable build
summary: The new video is maybe the most impressive yet, but it's the ending that spells potential trouble for Rockstar and Take-Two.
body: The great Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks continued today with a new video from Leek, and this one is particularly impressive, and damaging, because now it looks like the leaker really does have access to a playable build of the game. The bulk of the video shows a blue and yellow biplane flying over Vice City, and even as someone who's not a GTA fan I have to agree with posters on Reddit that it looks very impressive: Massive, detailed, and almost shockingly realistic. Cars can be seen moving on the streets and freeways below, even at great distances; you can't judge too much from a relatively low-resolution video posted on social media, but it looks smooth and steady, and there's virtually no discernable texture pop. There's also a few seconds spent with the in-game radio, a vital part of any GTA experience. I was a little disappointed that V-Rock got passed over (you never say "no" to Stevie Nicks) but there looks to be a nice variety of tunes on tap, as you'd expect. The kicker, though, comes at the end. Having exited his plane, our hero Jason takes a rifle and shoots the word "LEEK" into a wall. title: Screw the wedding photos, I'm playing Doom on a DSLR camera like the good lord intended
summary: Snap and tear? I got nuthin'.
body: The next time you spot someone earnestly fiddling with a DSLR camera at an event, sneak up behind them and take a look at what's going on onscreen. They could be deep in the settings menus—or potentially, blasting through a demon horde in Doom. Yes, it's time to chalk another device up on the "anything can play Doom if you try hard enough" board (via Tom's Hardware ). Github user Lauris-nl has built a module capable of running the game inside the open source Magic Lantern firmware , which in turn runs on the Canon EOS 550D digital SLR camera. The camera itself is an older model, originally released in 2010 and sometimes known as the Rebel T2i. The image processing hardware inside is apparently powerful enough to run Doom at a smooth frame rate, while the image adjustment and menu controls have been co-opted into what looks like a very playable configuration. You get your traditional up, down, left, and right buttons on the radial controls, while the Set button handles "select" and "fire" duties. You can also use the Menu button to, you guessed it, open the menu. It's like DSLR cameras were built for this. Okay, maybe not quite. Lauris-nl says the port is not intended for other cam…

title: AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D review
summary: Not a DIY play, but could be the basis for bundles and budget pre-built gaming PCs.
body: I'm trying not to be too down on the new(ish) AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D . After all, we are living in a time when the regular narrative is that all hardware is brutally overpriced and every tech company out there is trying to make a quick buck off the back of an AI bubble that is ever more certain to wipe out the global economy in one big pop . But here's AMD trying to give us an even more affordable AM5 gaming processor with a lovely dollop of the 3D V-Cache good-stuff. And yet I'm still not happy. I guess, fundamentally, I don't get it. You see, what we have here is a slightly slower Ryzen 7 7800X3D CPU with slightly lower MSRP. On the surface, that sounds great. The 7800X3D was the best gaming CPU of its generation, and only dropped off our recommended list when its Zen 5 replacement, the Ryzen 7 9800X3D , dropped in price. The issue is that the 7800X3D is old now. I reviewed it—very favourably I might add—back in April 2023. That in itself is not an issue; the underlying silicon is still excellent and still performs fantastically well up against the latest from either AMD or rivals Intel. The issue is that it's been out in the market a long while, most enthusiasts have their eyes on…

body: One tragedy about the fall of Arkane Austin—aside from Microsoft's seeming unwillingness to give studios a chance beyond the next quarter—is the pervasive feeling that the studio, whose devs were previously known for their immersive sims, was forced to make something way outside of their wheelhouse. Redfall was a live service shooter, and a pretty cruddy one at that. So it might be buoying news to hear that Dishonored co-creator Harvey Smith and seasoned Arkane vet Ben Horne's new studio isn't going to try and chase down trends. In an interview with The Game Business , Horne and Smith were asked if they thought the immersive sim (which Black Pony Immersive has been strangely careful to talk around), is a dead or dying genre. "If you look back through those games," says Smith, "There are a lot of titles that people still talk about 10 or 20 years later. They have a lot of cultural cachet. And there are a few, if you look at BioShock or Deus Ex or Dishonored, that make a lot of money." body: This month, the biggest leveraged buyout in the history of private equity went through and now EA is owned by a consortium made up of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and the investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners. Will that change the way it does business or encourage it to rely on the formula that's gotten it where it is? I asked Emmanuel Rosier, director of market intelligence at industry analysts Newzoo , who spent nine years as a senior manager at EA. "I think everything is open at this point," Rosier says. "I suspect that sports will remain the key focus for EA, particularly European football, soccer, because of the importance of that sport in Saudi and in Middle East territories. You see a lot of synergies in that context. You can also expect that they will push even more for esports, also given the popularity of esports in Saudi and in some other territories. title: Sony reportedly reverses course on live service co-op Horizon game after 'negative player feedback'
summary: The spinoff has been undergoing a rework since June.
body: The developers at Guerilla Games are making a last-minute pivot for their live service co-op game set in the Horizon universe after receiving negative player feedback during recent playtests, Bloomberg reports. Horizon Hunters Gathering was supposed to be a live service co-op action game where you group up as a team of animated heroes and fight mechanical beasts. Players reacted poorly to it over the three playtests earlier this year—one of which had to compete with Marathon's server slam weekend that was going on at the same time. Instead of pulling the plug on it, like Sony has done to several live service games , it gave the studio several months to reboot it into a regular co-op game with a story and a smaller scope. According to Bloomberg's sources, Sony told the team earlier today that it will need to impress executives with their next milestone in December. If it fails to wow anyone by then, Horizon Hunters Gathering might join the graveyard of canceled live service Sony games. title: GTA 6 cars need gas? OK, I'm finally on board

body: Grab a bucket, because GTA 6 is springing leaks in every direction. A group (individual?) called Cyberleek has been publishing seemingly genuine clips from Rockstar's latest for two days now, giving us our first glimpses of gameplay a week ahead of the big Netflix reveal happening on August 27. There's electricity in the air around GTA 6—easily the most anticipated game in history—but I wasn't actually excited to play it until yesterday, when one of the leaked clips (which we won't be linking here, but isn't difficult to find) showed Jason, one of the game's dual protagonists, climbing into a car. As he takes control, the UI shows what seems to be status symbols for the vehicle: its HP and its current gas. Heeeelllllll yea. I hope you actually have to pull up to a gas pump and remember which side the tank is on. I hope you can stash a spare canister in the trunk, and I hope that canister will violently explode if it eats a bullet. (Image credit: Rockstar) Systems. Simulations! This is exactly the stuff that GTA needs to meaningfully evolve. body: Saudi Arabia's purchase of Electronic Arts, the biggest leveraged buyout in private equity history, officially closed earlier this month . With that deal done, a new Game Developer report has found that an awful lot of employees are expecting much more stringent control over what kinds of games they are and are not allowed to make. This isn't really new, strictly speaking. After the buyout was announced, current and former EA employees alike expressed concerns about a potential crackdown on some games, particularly those that are visibly diverse and inclusive, like The Sims. Former BioWare lead writer Trick Weekes summed it up aptly , predicting that "guns and football" will be fine, but that "gay stuff" will likely be out. title: I modded GTA 5's NPCs to be punishable for their crimes, and also much more polite
summary: Oh, and I still keep falling asleep in the middle of the road.
body: Los Santos Customs I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier . Grand Theft Auto 6 will, I am assured, have the greatest NPCs of all time. They will be perfect human simulacra, indistinguishable from the meaty lifeforms behind the controller. My goal: to make GTA 5's barely-living NPCs an approximation of that. So I installed two mods: NPC Check On Player and NPCs Get Wanted Stars . The former makes the citizens of Los Santos more polite—they will get out of their cars and check you are okay if they run you over. The latter makes them punishable when they are impolite—when they commit crimes, they will earn their own wanted stars, and find themselves pursued by cops. Stop in the name of the law. (Image credit: Rockstar) I'll be honest, I mostly installed the NPC Check mod because I hoped it would compel them to stand still when they got wanted stars from hurting me, but hey, it does what it says on the tin. title: Overwatch's newest Emerald rank is like a live grenade wedged between plat and diamond
summary: Godspeed to all those hardstuck.
body: Overwatch season 4 introduced a rank reset and you know what that means, it's every cat, hog, and retired sniper for themselves as players desperately try to claw back to where they finished last season. As if that isn't stressful enough, we've also got a new rank on our hands. Slotted between ranks Platinum and Diamond you can now find Emerald, the answer to the growing skill disparity between Plat and Diamond players. "As we've shown in the past, the majority of our players are in Gold and Platinum," the patch notes read . "So adding a new rank closer to the middle of the skill curve gives many players a better sense of rank identity, a new goal to achieve, and increases fidelity in assessing skill for many players." (Image credit: Blizzard) Season 4 is full of really smart changes, and this new rank is one of them. I completely agree that there needed to be a buffer between Plat and Diamond, as high plat and low diamond increasingly became a frantic free-for-all with players who had vastly different skills far too frequently grouped together. But the tradeoff seems to be that all this chaos is now neatly packed into Emerald. I only played in a few Emerald games when I was placi…

title: Dishonored co-creator Harvey Smith launches a new studio and it literally has the word 'Immersive' in the name
summary: Just in case there's any confusion, Black Pony Immersive's website also drops a reference to Looking Glass Studios.
body: Former Arkane Austin studio director Harvey Smith, known for his work on games including Deus Ex, Thief: Deadly Shadows, and Dishonored, has joined with executive producer Ben Horne to launch a new studio called Black Pony Immersive. The new operation features "an elite development team" built around personnel from Arkane, Insomniac, Epic, Avalanche, and Volition, including Smith's long-time collaborator Ricardo Bare. In case the name Black Pony Immersive doesn't give it away, the new studio is "built to design and develop imaginative first person action RPGs set within well-realized worlds," with emergent game systems giving players the freedom to approach challenges as they see fit. And if you're thinking to yourself, boy, that sure seems like a lot of words to say 'immersive sims, ' well, you're right. But immersive sims are in kind of a rough place right now, so I don't blame Smith and company for taking a more verbose, descriptive run at laying out what they want to do. "During a time of industry volatility, I'm proud to announce the next step in my videogame journey with the reveal of our new studio," Smith said."This effort reflects everything we've learned, and all we hold…

title: Kioxia Exceria Pro G2 NVMe SSD review
summary: You gotta respect the hustle.
body: I vehemently dislike reviewing laptops. I know that's a weird sentence to start an SSD review off with, but humor me for a second. Basically, the configuration you get is never correct. You go "oh hi X manufacturer, this laptop looks great, can you send me a sample for review?" and they go "yeah, sure, this is the model" and it'll arrive on your doorstep, and it's some weird hybrid amped up special edition with extra RAM, a different storage setup, and a screen that you can't find anywhere else except from some odd retailer eseller based in the Seychelles, for some reason. At that point you'll then proceed to spend the next three hours of your life trying to source a price for the thing that's even remotely similar to the one you have, and then scream because without a price tag reviewing the thing becomes damn near impossible. Sadly, in the last year or so, SSD reviewing has followed a remarkably similar path. 33% of the time the SSD you get, doesn't have the same NAND and controller that it actually launched with, 33% of the time its price has been ricocheting back and forth to the point it doesn't resemble anything close to the launch price, and the remaining 33% of the time ma…

title: Keychron K8 Ultra 8K review
summary: Solid, dependable and versatile.
body: Keychron has carved out a wonderful niche in the now admittedly overcrowded mechanical keyboard space for offering fantastic all-round keyboards with all the features and robustness you could want for a surprisingly affordable price, given what's on offer. The new K8 Ultra 8K might feel like I'm parroting a lot of the same thoughts as I have with the numerous other Keychron products I've tested simply because most products I've tested from them have been consistently excellent. This new model doesn't deviate from a lot of the established formula: hefty aluminium top case, PBT keycaps, versatile connectivity, web-based software. And let me tell you, that's no bad thing. Okay, against the likes of the Lemokey L4 and Keychron Q3 Max , I can nitpick and say the entire case isn't the usual machined aluminium as there's a doubleshot ABS portion on the underside mated to an aluminium top piece. However, that is nitpicking of the highest order. The K8 Ultra 8K remains the type of keyboard you could use as a weapon. It's 1.2 kg in heft, which is a lot for a smaller form factor keyboard, and has a fantastically sturdy frame to boot. To go with it, we've also got the usual doubleshot PBT key…

title: The Blood of Dawnwalker's final system requirements include upscaling set to Balanced—so unsurprisingly, they're lower
summary: Who would've thought?
body: Squinting at the new The Blood of Dawnwalker system requirements this morning before my second cup of coffee, my bleary eyes registered that the listed GPUs are often significantly less powerful than the previous recommended specs . As my tired eyeballs came into focus, though, it became clear why: upscaling, of course. Rebel Wolves has taken into account the modern inventions of DLSS, FSR, and XeSS in its final specs sheet. A reply to the X thread from the official account reveals that the new specs are based on Balanced upscaling settings , which would account for some of the drops. Why the Balanced setting wasn't clearly stated on the specs image and left for a thread reply to clear up is beyond me. Anyway, for 1080p 30 fps gameplay, Rebel Wolves now recommends an Intel Core i5 11400F or AMD Ryzen 7 2700X, alongside 16 GB of RAM and an Nvidia GTX 1060 or AMD Radeon RX 580 . For 1080p Medium settings at 60 fps, you're looking at an RTX 2060 Super , a GTX 1070 Ti, an RX 5700 , or the Intel Arc A750 , along with significantly chonkier CPUs. For 1440p High settings, the specs jump significantly to an Intel Core i7 11700K or AMD Ryzen 7 5700X , and an RTX 4060, RX 7600 XT, or Intel …

title: Subnautica 2's latest 1.2 update is friend focused—finally adding the key mechanic to any great multiplayer game
summary: Nothing's impossible when you have the power of friendship.
body: I'm not sure there's been a better invention for multiplayer games than proximity chat. Whether it be friends screaming vengeance down the side of a mountain after you abandon them in Peak , or the wails of one of your fellow workers fall suspiciously silent in Lethal Company . Proximity chat offers up fertile ground for hilariously wacky and memorable multiplayer moments, so you can imagine my excitement when I found out it's coming to Subnautica 2 . "This is going to let you have an in-game voice chat option that you can do with your friends," Anthony Gallegos, creative director, says in a dev diary . "You'll be able to talk locally with each other and then as you get further away you'll hear a switch to sort of a radio-sounding voice, and you'll progressively break up as you get further away, up until a certain point where you can almost not hear me at all." Now, you can use your friends as a canary, sending them down into dark caves and listening to see if anything's amiss. At the very least, Gallegos believes it will "definitely add to the tension of" exploring the formidable alien ocean. But that's not all being added to Subnautica 2 in its next update. The whole patch seems…

title: Fired Rockstar workers say you shouldn't boycott GTA 6 for them: 'We spent years pouring our hard work, skill, and creativity into making GTA'
summary: "That doesn't mean we want you to let Rockstar off the hook."
body: Rockstar's been embroiled for some time in a legal dispute after firing 30 unionised workers in the UK , which has, naturally, been seen as union-busting behaviour by those impacted. The workers, who are part of The Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB), have been making solid progress. In June of this year, it was decided that IWGB would be allowed to present its case that Rockstar had allegedly blacklisted its unionised employees —as in, compiled a list of union members—which would be in violation of The Employment Relations Act , which plainly states that you can't compile a "details of persons who are or have been members of trade unions" for the purposes of "treating a person less favourably than another on grounds of trade union membership or trade union activities." The full trial will be held in September, but in the meantime, the IWGB has stated that folks excited for GTA 6 don't have to boycott the game on their behalf. In a recent video , fired employees stated: "We're going to make it easy for you. Don't boycott GTA 6, win justice for the people who helped make it. "We spent years pouring our hard work, skill, and creativity into making GTA. And we want peo…

title: GTA 6 leaks show a game that looks like more GTA, but not a revolution
summary: It sure doesn't look like the reinvention of the wheel(s).
body: The exciting thing about Rockstar games is not that they have the most advanced technology behind them, the best stories, or the most avant-garde game systems. It's the extraordinary amount of work the studio invests into the little details that make up its big worlds. Red Dead Redemption's dynamic horse testicles (they shrink when it's cold) are a frequently-cited example of that commitment to the particulars. A pair of videos purported to be leaked GTA 6 gameplay surfaced online today , and if they are legit (the immediate copyright takedowns suggest as much), they seem to confirm that GTA 6 is more of the same. The short clips obviously can't express the full scope of Rockstar's designs—and we don't know how recent they are—but there's nothing in them to indicate that GTA 6 will reinvent the open-world crime spree. In one, the player shoots some hoops as protagonist Jason. It's cool that a basketball on the ground and a hoop nailed to the side of your house are not just static props. There's a system in place for shooting accurately, and the game tracks the number of shots made. The other clip is a very typical GTA scene: The player makes a reckless turn in a car, gets clipped …

title: Industry legend Warren Spector is retiring: 'I'm feeling like I've done what I set out to do'
summary: The man who helped give us Ultima Underworld, System Shock, Deus Ex, and Epic Mickey is riding off into the sunset.
body: Warren Spector is one of the industry's most storied developers, particularly among fans of immersive sims. His leading roles on games like Ultima Underworld , System Shock , and Deus Ex —and you know what, even Invisible War and Deadly Shadows , which are probably better than you think—established him as one of the field's most admired and enduring names. And now, after doing it for more than 40 years, he's calling it a day. "Let me cut right to the chase. I'm retiring from game development," Spector wrote on LinkedIn . "At least I think so. I've been here before and changed my mind but this time I'm pretty sure I mean it." Spector said he's had a "great career" and wouldn't change a thing, but added that he's coming up on 44 years as a developer, a span that's seen him work on tabletop RPGs, board games, and "more digital games than [he] can remember," as part of teams ranging in size from a dozen people to 800. "I've worked for big companies and done startups," he wrote. "I like to think I've helped some insanely talented people along in their careers. (That last is the most important.) "With all that behind me and with age and health (my business) catching up with me I'm feeli…

title: 'Live-service is a red flag for us': Why one publisher is embracing an older kind of multiplayer hit: peer-to-peer, server browsers, and organic community
summary: Tripwire sees preservation as a responsibility.
body: It's a frustrating thing to watch good games disappear. We've seen it happen time and time and time again: studios spend years on a cool multiplayer thing, bank on it being popular enough to become a live-service hit, then toss the entire project into the trash when that doesn't happen. That could have been the fate of Deceive Inc , a 2023 'PvP Hitman' shooter that has attracted a passionate, but small community. Developer Sweet Bandits supported the game with substantial updates and microtransactions for over a year, but unfortunately shut down in 2024, leaving fans to assume Deceive Inc would one day disappear, too. Then last month, the unexpected happened : an update on its Steam page announced that not only would Deceive Inc not be going offline, but work is underway on community server tools and mod support that will essentially give the game to the community, and keep it playable forever. The update is not the work of Sweet Bandits, but an initiative of Deceive Inc's publisher, Tripwire Interactive.
